subject: vt-dy
title: VT.DY.-----DIS.C.CT.
description: First of two diagrams in MP(II)-11. The crossing diagrams how vibrational-dynamics structurally meets disconnect — the structural mechanism Braxton names when transfer-cycle creativity gets disconnected from its source-region's actual vibrational ground. VT-DY (vibrational dynamics — what the form's actual vibrational working consists of) is crossed with DIS-C-CT (disconnect — the partner-side's mechanism for severing the form from its vibrational ground). VT-DY sits on the left with the subject-arrow; TR (transformation) rises above and EXP-DY (exposure dynamics) sits at upper-right, with T-C-IMP (temporal-continuity implication) below EXP-DY routing into INFO-COMP (information composite), AFN (affinity natural), and IF-SPT (isolated-focus spectacle) on the right margin as the partner-side's downward chain. POL-DY (political dynamics) sits at center-left as the subject's downward output, with POL-P (political particulars), PART (participation), and ECO-DYM (economic dynamism) clustered at the bottom-left as the subject's downward chain. Structural argument: when vibrational-dynamics is crossed with disconnect, the upper diagonal TR → EXP-DY → T-C-IMP → INFO-COMP → AFN → IF-SPT is the *disconnection-route* the State Department's transfer cycles produce — transformation routes through exposure-dynamics into temporal-continuity-implication, then through information-composite into affinity-natural, terminating in isolated-focus spectacle. The form's vibrational-dynamics gets converted into spectacle on the partner-side. POL-DY → POL-P → PART / ECO-DYM on the lower-left is what vibrational-dynamics produces on its own when the upper diagonal absorbs the form — political-dynamics routes into political-particulars and participation, but reduced to economic-dynamism as the lower terminus. The disconnect is structural: the upper chain's mechanisms hand the form's vibrational-dynamics off as spectacle without ever letting it reach the lower-left's actual political-participation.
